_source: Hand-authored from docs/research/2026-09-07-jd-skill-taxonomy-{ml,fde-craft,infrastructure}.md and the benchmark spec sections 4 and 6. No model writes this file at runtime; only the counting is automated. Row numbers are Plan-sheet rows: row N = workbook.json['Plan'][N] = curriculum.json topics key N-1. Every primaryRow, supportRow and nearestRow below was checked against that sheet.
_rules: Skills are capability terms, never title terms. 'Applied AI' is deliberately absent: it is a job-title string that means customer-facing at Mistral and core research at Perplexity, and matching it would pull in Databricks and Perplexity postings that are not FDE work. Title classification belongs in lib/market/classify.ts, not here.
Matching is boolean per requisition - presence, not occurrence count.

A skill named only inside a mission statement or an EEO block must not count. Boilerplate stripping runs before matching (static per-company blocks plus the automatic 60%-of-a-company's-postings line rule), and the exclude[] lists here are the second line of defence for the phrases that survive it - benefits blocks ('healthcare coverage', 'travel stipend', 'onsite meals'), EEO blocks ('in compliance with applicable law'), and role-description filler ('scope of the role', 'prompt communication').

minDistinctForms > 1 is set for every skill whose single surface form is commonly boilerplate: a lone 'LLM', 'agent', 'cost', 'monitoring', 'compliance', 'documentation', 'healthcare', 'scope', 'stakeholder', 'docker' or 'machine learning' mention does not fire the skill.
Gaps carry statedFrequency verbatim from the audited taxonomy. The system never infers that a gap exists; it only reports a mapping a human already checked against all 2,236 subtopics.
proximity.window is in characters, measured either side of the hit.

gaps.label: Codifying field patterns back into Product and Research
gaps.whyNotCovered: Plan coverage is per-artifact templating only: row 73's reusable discovery script, row 80's 'Sanitise, templatise and test the pack on real readers', row 74's docs-as-code templates, row 20's golden pipeline for every customer repo, row 66's two-API adapter as a reusable asset. Nothing teaches the pattern library, the accelerator, or the structured route from a field observation to a product or research input.
gaps.statedFrequency: 12 of 15 craft-corpus reqs (80%), 4 of 4 companies - the highest-frequency bullet in the corpus with the weakest plan match

gaps.label: Pre-sales technical account leadership (use-case portfolio, proof of value, adoption plan, technical win)
gaps.whyNotCovered: Zero hits across 2,236 subtopics for use-case portfolio, proof of value, technical win, land and expand, consumption, adoption plan, technical account plan, expansion, renewal or account health. Row 73 teaches discovery and row 75 teaches demos; neither teaches the account-plan motion.
gaps.statedFrequency: 5 of 15 craft-corpus reqs (33%), but 5 of 5 Architect- and SE-titled reqs, which carry the top compensation bands in the corpus

gaps.label: Value measurement and ROI instrumentation
gaps.whyNotCovered: The cost side is deep (row 21's CFO page, row 65's customer-facing unit-economics number, row 75's unit-economics sheet). The benefit side has no home. Nearest coverage is one subtopic in row 84, 'From "we want AI" to a falsifiable outcome metric with a baseline', which stops at metric definition and never reaches pre- and post-deployment measurement or reporting to an executive sponsor.

gaps.label: Customer enablement, workshops and training delivery
gaps.whyNotCovered: Row 74's handover pack teaches proving the customer can operate what you built; nothing teaches teaching them to build. The only 'workshop' strings in the plan are incidental - row 56's injection payloads 'you can reproduce from memory in a customer workshop' and row 64's prompt edit 'made in a customer workshop'.

gaps.label: Named agent and orchestration frameworks (LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, Agents SDK, DSPy)
gaps.whyNotCovered: Zero hits for LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, Agents SDK or Claude Agent SDK; LangChain and LlamaIndex appear twice, incidentally, in rows 62 and 64. Rows 52, 53 and 57 teach the mechanics these frameworks wrap and row 57 builds a real agent, so this is a vocabulary and name-recognition gap, not a capability gap - it costs keyword screens, not interviews.
gaps.statedFrequency: 9 of 95 postings (9%) say 'agent frameworks'; 2 of 17 in the infrastructure corpus name the category explicitly

gaps.label: Voice and speech agents (ASR, TTS, turn-taking, real-time audio latency budgets)
gaps.whyNotCovered: Zero hits for Whisper, ASR, text-to-speech, speech recognition or voice agent. Every 'voice' and 'speech' match in the plan is tone-of-voice prose or security-briefing text. Row 35 gives the SSE and WebSocket streaming transport half only; no audio pipeline, no turn-taking, no barge-in.
gaps.statedFrequency: 8 of 95 postings (8%), 3 companies (Sierra, Decagon, Scale) - concentrated in the CX-agent vendor segment, absent from OpenAI and Anthropic FDE postings

gaps.label: Managed cloud AI platforms as deployment targets (Bedrock, Vertex AI, Azure AI Foundry, SageMaker)
gaps.whyNotCovered: Zero hits for SageMaker, Vertex AI, Azure OpenAI or Azure AI Foundry. Bedrock appears in five rows but only incidentally - a bedrock-runtime VPC endpoint in row 15, Bedrock Guardrails as one moderation option in row 56, renamed models in row 60's cost attribution, an exception-mapping example in row 61, constrained decoding in row 66. No row teaches deploying a frontier model through a hyperscaler surface, which is how Claude is actually bought by regulated enterprises.
gaps.statedFrequency: 0 of 95 postings name the AI services; 5 of 17 in the infrastructure corpus name the clouds - a field-reality gap, not a keyword gap

gaps.label: Knowledge graphs, GraphRAG and ontology modelling
gaps.whyNotCovered: Zero hits for knowledge graph, Neo4j, Cypher, GraphRAG or ontology anywhere in the 119 topics. Row 119 is graph machine learning - message passing, GCN and GAT derivations, GraphSAGE, 1-WL expressivity, R-GCN over a CRM schema - which is graph learning, not graph-backed retrieval. Row 38 is entity resolution, adjacent but not a KG build.

gaps.label: Partner, SI and prime-contractor orchestration
gaps.whyNotCovered: Zero hits for systems integrator, prime contractor, teaming agreement, reseller or marketplace; 'partner' appears only as a job title inside row 91's title taxonomy. Nothing teaches managing or negotiating teaming agreements with Tier 1 primes, or coordinating delivery through a partner.
gaps.statedFrequency: 3 of 15 craft-corpus reqs (20%), but structurally load-bearing above senior

gaps.label: Delivery-team leadership, mentoring and hiring
gaps.whyNotCovered: The plan has row 88's Story 9, 'Leadership without authority' - a rehearsed three-minute interview answer, not a craft topic. Nothing teaches coaching junior engagement managers, acting as the go-to resource on complex projects, or participating in hiring.
gaps.statedFrequency: 4 of 15 craft-corpus reqs (27%) - exactly the Senior-to-Lead boundary

gaps.label: EMEA and AI-specific regulatory frameworks (DORA, NIS2, ISO 42001, EU AI Act, ZDR)
gaps.whyNotCovered: EU AI Act appears exactly once across 2,236 subtopics, inside row 71's 'The LLM-specific compliance surface'. DORA: zero. NIS2: zero. ISO 42001: zero. Zero Data Retention as a contract construct: zero.
gaps.statedFrequency: 1 of 15 craft-corpus reqs (7%) - narrow, but that posting is the GBP 190-230k Anthropic Applied AI Security Architect and its entire premise is this vocabulary

gaps.label: Conversation and dialogue design for CX agents
gaps.whyNotCovered: Zero real hits for conversation design, dialogue design, chatbot design or deflection as a discipline. The four matches are false positives: negotiation deflection in rows 77 and 92, row 78's 'the artifact you build here is a timer plus an immutable audit trail, not a chatbot', and row 84's metric-trap note that deflection measured as no-follow-up-ticket scores abandoned, angry users as successes.
gaps.statedFrequency: Concentrated in Sierra and Decagon; near-zero at OpenAI, Anthropic and Scale. Worth closing only if Sierra/Decagon/Parloa-class companies are on the target list

gaps.label: Public-sector acquisition and authorization (ATO, 3PAO, SSP, OTA, program of record)
gaps.whyNotCovered: FedRAMP appears three times - rows 27, 74 and 81 - but only as an access-constraint label, never as an authorization process. Zero hits for ATO, 3PAO, SSP, RFP, RFI, OTA, program of record or capture. The taxonomy calls this a correct omission rather than a defect: these roles are US-citizen-and-clearance gated, and row 81's 'Customer-site reality: access, security and the trips you cannot take' already teaches filtering them out.

gaps.label: Synthetic data generation and eval-data manufacture at volume
gaps.whyNotCovered: Dataset construction is covered - row 55's chat template and loss masking, row 117's non-leaking held-out split, row 59's 200-case sampling frame with stratification and provenance - so training-data quality is not a gap. What is missing is generating synthetic training and eval data at volume; the only 'synthetic data' hit in the plan is row 89, about seeded screenshot data for portfolio images.
gaps.statedFrequency: About 5 of 95 postings (5%), Scale only - the lowest-priority ML gap

gaps.label: Knowledge distillation and small-language-model optimisation
gaps.whyNotCovered: Two hits for distillation, small language model or model optimisation, both in row 99 and both incidental (label smoothing and KL). Quantisation is covered in row 62 and 'use a smaller model' is covered as economics in row 65's cascade routing, but student-teacher distillation is absent.
gaps.statedFrequency: 1 of 17 in the infrastructure corpus (6%), one Scale posting

gaps.label: Eval and observability SaaS breadth (LangSmith, Braintrust, Arize/Phoenix, Ragas, W&B Weave)
gaps.whyNotCovered: The plan standardises on promptfoo (rows 56 and 59), Langfuse (rows 51, 60, 64) and MLflow (row 64). LangSmith, Braintrust, Arize/Phoenix, Ragas and W&B Weave: zero hits. No JD names an eval vendor, so this is a conversational-fluency gap only.
gaps.statedFrequency: 0 of 17 in the infrastructure corpus - no posting names an eval vendor

gaps.label: Feature stores
gaps.whyNotCovered: Zero hits in the plan. Also zero in the JD corpus. Recorded for completeness of the audit; the taxonomy's own judgement is that it is not worth closing.
gaps.statedFrequency: 0 of 17 in the infrastructure corpus - not worth closing

overInvested.measuredJdFrequency: 1 of 95 postings (1%) - a single Scale public-sector line, 'deploying deep learning solutions'. Across the whole corpus: XGBoost 0, scikit-learn 0, LightGBM 0, SHAP 0, LIME 0, anomaly and fraud detection 0, time series 0, recommenders 0.
overInvested.note: Track N, Machine Learning Systems. Defensible as depth behind the answer - row 104's calibration, leakage and metric-choice material is what makes row 59's eval work credible - but it will not be recognised by a keyword screen and will not be asked about directly. Not defensible as scheduled hours in months 18-22 if loops start earlier.

overInvested.measuredJdFrequency: 0 of 95 postings. PyTorch 0, TensorFlow 0, computer vision 0, GPU 0, vLLM 0, TensorRT 0, Triton 0, quantisation 0.
overInvested.note: Track O, Deep Learning and Multimodal. Row 116 (build a small GPT) is what makes row 50's answers load-bearing, and row 117 is far deeper than the 2-of-17 fine-tuning ask, but the surface language matches nothing in this market. The rows that match 14 of 17 of the market - 59 evals, 53 agents, 54 RAG, 60 observability, 65 cost and latency - sit at months 13-15.

overInvested.measuredJdFrequency: 0 of 95 postings. No linear algebra, calculus, probability, Bayes, statistical inference, hypothesis testing, confidence interval, entropy or information theory vocabulary appears anywhere in the corpus.
overInvested.note: Track M, Mathematical Foundations. Rows 98 (A/B design and power) and 104 pair up behind the eval work, and row 100 pairs with row 28's Python, so the track is not wasted. But no posting in the corpus asks for any of it by name, and it is scheduled across months 2-11 against a zero-signal surface.
